rows.question: What is the minimum attendance required at LPU?

rows.question: Which textbook is used for Computer Organization and Architecture?
rows.answer: Textbook: Computer Organization and Design: The Hardware/Software Interface (Patterson and Hennessy, 5th edition). [1] References: Computer Organisation and Architecture (Smruti Ranjan Sarangi); Computer System Architecture (Mano); Computer Organization and Embedded Systems (Hamacher, 6th edition); Computer Architecture and Organization (Hayes, 3rd edition); Computer Organization and Architecture: Designing for Performance (Stallings, 10th edition); Computer System Design and Architecture (Heuring and Jordan, 2nd edition). [1] The AICTE Computer Organization and Architecture syllabus covers five modules: an introduction (von Neumann model, performance, data representation), the RISC-V instruction set architecture, the processor (data path, control and pipelining), the memory hierarchy (caches and DRAM), and storage and I/O (disks, flash, interrupts and DMA). [2]

rows.question: What topics are covered in the Computer Networks syllabus?
rows.answer: The AICTE Computer Networks syllabus covers eight modules: an introduction to the Internet, the application layer (DNS, HTTP, SMTP), Linux socket programming, the transport layer (TCP, UDP, congestion control), the IP layer (IPv4, IPv6, NAT, firewalls), routing protocols (link state, distance vector, OSPF, BGP), the data link layer (CRC, CSMA/CD, Ethernet, ARP), and wireless networks (802.11). [1] The AICTE Operating Systems syllabus covers seven modules: an introduction to operating systems, a computer organization refresher, processes and system calls, memory management and virtual memory, process management and CPU scheduling, concurrency and synchronization (threads, locks, semaphores, deadlocks), and file systems. [2]

rows.question: What does the Theory of Computation syllabus cover?
rows.answer: The AICTE Theory of Computation syllabus covers three modules: finite automata and regular languages (DFA, NFA, regular expressions, pumping lemma), context-free grammars and pushdown automata, and Turing machines, decidability and complexity (P, NP and EXP). [1] This is the Theory of Computation (automata theory) syllabus from the AICTE Model Curriculum for the UG degree in Computer Science and Engineering (revised 2022), published by AICTE, the All India Council for Technical Education. [2]

rows.question: What are the modules in the Design and Analysis of Algorithms syllabus?
rows.answer: The AICTE Design and Analysis of Algorithms syllabus covers six modules: applications of graph search (BFS and DFS), greedy algorithms, divide and conquer, dynamic programming and shortest paths, network flows, and intractability (P, NP and NP-completeness). [1] Textbooks: Algorithm Design (Kleinberg and Tardos); Algorithms (Dasgupta, Papadimitriou and Vazirani); Design and Analysis of Algorithms (Gajendra Sharma, 4th edition, Khanna). [2] References: Introduction to Algorithms (Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, 4th edition); Algorithm Design: Foundations, Analysis, and Internet Examples (Goodrich and Tamassia, 2nd edition). [2]

rows.question: What topics are in the Compiler Design syllabus?
rows.answer: The AICTE Compiler Design syllabus covers eight modules: an introduction to compilers, lexical analysis (LEX and Flex), syntax analysis and parsing (LR or LL), semantic analysis, syntax-directed translation to three-address code, run-time support (activation records and calls), an introduction to code optimization, and code generation. [1]

rows.question: What is the Software Engineering course outline about?
rows.answer: The AICTE Software Engineering course covers the iterative software development process, project planning, requirements including the user interface, architecture and design, coding with modern IDEs, testing, and integration and deployment, applied in a team software project. [1] This is the Software Engineering course outline from the AICTE Model Curriculum for the UG degree in Computer Science and Engineering (revised 2022), published by AICTE, the All India Council for Technical Education. [2] Unlike the core subjects, AICTE gives Software Engineering only as a short outline, without module-wise units, weekly hours or textbooks. [2]
